newsitem.title: USA: Most IMM currencies higher in light, subdued trade.
newsitem.headline: Most IMM currencies higher in light, subdued trade.

text.p: IMM currency futures were mostly higher, but key currencies remained below GLOBEX highs after Japanese officials calmed dollar selling by the time U.S. markets opened, traders and analysts said.

Japanese Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka told reporters that excessive strengthening of the yen as well as a a weakening was undesirable. He also said the Group of Seven's (G7) communique calling for currency stability was still valid.
The comments helped cap September yen's early pit gains at $0.009134, below the GLOBEX high of $0.009174.

September yen's overnight high was the contract's highest level since it reached $0.009165 on December 9, 1996. Further resistance is at the December 5, 1996 high of $0.009260, which also corresponds to a key retracement level, analysts said.

September yen has retraced more than 62 percent of its 10-month downmove after rallying through $0.009163 overnight, some noted. The contract then knocked through resistance at $0.009167-69 after the dollar/yen hit sell-stops and fell to 110.62 spot yen.
They said U.S. deputy Treasury secretary Lawrence Summers' comments were the catalyst for the strong move.

Summers said Japan should avoid running up external surpluses that would hurt global growth. His statements fed the current belief that the U.S. administration may use the dollar as a trade policy tool, traders said.

On Tuesday, U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky expressed concern about "disturbing trends" in Japan's trade balance and repeated that the United States does not want a big rise in Japan's surplus.
Japan's current account surplus rose more than 90 percent to 1.09 trillion yen in April from a year earlier.
Mitsuzuka said Japan's current account surplus will be a topic at the June 20-22 G7 meeting in Denver.

September yen rallied through 5-3/4-month highs on Tuesday on ideas Japan's surplus would show an even stronger rise. However, the rally was contained on fears of central bank intervention on behalf of the dollar.
Such intervention fears were also noted in the futures pits on Wednesday morning.

At 0816 CDT/1316 GMT, September yen was up $0.000095 at $0.009124, marks rose $0.0010 at $0.5870, Swiss francs were $0.0030 higher at $0.7047, sterling fell $0.0008 at $1.6342, Canadian dollars were up $0.0004 at $0.7262, Australian dollars were $0.0042 lower at $0.7585 and Mexican pesos were $0.000100 higher at $0.120200.
